text: Why does time seem to fly faster every year?
When you're five, one year is a fifth of your whole life. At fifty, it's just one fiftieth.
Kids are full of firsts: first day of school, first trip, first everything.
New experiences leave lots of detailed memories, so looking back, that time feels long.
But routine blurs together. Same week, same commute, and your brain stores less.
So want time to slow down? Do something new.
When did you last do something for the first time?
